seo.title: Rabat Travel Guide 2026 | Capital, Kasbah & Atlantic Coast | MoroccoTripMap
seo.description: Rabat guide: Kasbah of the Udayas, Hassan Tower, Chellah, medina, Bouregreg marina and Atlantic beach. When to go, where to stay and how to explore the capital.

name: Rabat
hero_subtitle: Morocco’s Atlantic capital — Kasbah cliffs, Hassan Tower, Chellah and the Bouregreg waterfront.

info.area_val: Historic walls, red brick and Bouregreg calm

overview.title: A capital you can still explore on foot
overview.p1: Rabat sits where the Bouregreg meets the Atlantic: the white-and-blue Kasbah of the Udayas above the estuary, the unfinished Hassan Tower and Mausoleum of Mohammed V, the Roman–Marinid ruins of Chellah, and a medina easier than Fez or Marrakech. A green, ordered political capital, kept from pure bureaucracy by ocean breeze and estuary light.
overview.p2: Two or three days cover the kasbah, Hassan complex, Chellah, the medina and a marina or beach walk. Day trips run to Salé across the river, Casablanca or the coast toward Kenitra. Stay near the medina, Hassan or Agdal depending on the mood you want.

places.title: Must-visit places in Rabat
places.subtitle: Kasbah, tower, necropolis, medina and Bouregreg shore.

oudayas.title: Kasbah of the Udayas
oudayas.desc: White-and-blue quarter above the estuary with Andalusian gardens.

hassan.title: Hassan Tower
hassan.desc: Iconic Almohad minaret and unfinished mosque esplanade.

mausoleum.title: Mausoleum of Mohammed V
mausoleum.desc: Marble and zellige monument beside Hassan Tower.

chellah.title: Chellah
chellah.desc: Roman and Marinid necropolis in a walled garden above the Bouregreg.

medina.title: Rabat medina
medina.desc: Compact lanes, souks and walls toward the ocean.

gardens.title: Andalusian Gardens
gardens.desc: Shaded gardens inside the Kasbah of the Udayas.

marina.title: Bouregreg Marina
marina.desc: Modern marina and promenade facing Salé.

beach.title: Rabat beach
beach.desc: Atlantic sand under the walls and along the corniche.

museum.title: Rabat museums
museum.desc: Archaeology and modern collections in the capital.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day outline
itinerary.subtitle: Kasbah and Hassan first, then Chellah and the waterfront.

detailed_itinerary.day1_m: Morning — Kasbah of the Udayas & gardens
detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Kasbah of the Udayas and Andalusian gardens — views over the Bouregreg and the Atlantic.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Explore the medina, Rue des Consuls and a café stop near the historic walls.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Sunset from an Udayas terrace, then a Moroccan dinner in the medina.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Visit the Hassan Tower esplanade and the marble Mausoleum of Mohammed V.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Walk the Roman and Marinid ruins and gardens of Chellah.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Evening stroll at Bouregreg Marina or dinner with a river view.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Museums or a traditional boat crossing to old Salé.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Rabat beach or corniche time, with free time in Agdal cafés.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Last mint tea in the kasbah or a final dinner facing the estuary.

stays.title: Where to stay in Rabat? Our favorites
stays.subtitle: Hotels near Hassan Tower and the Kasbah, a practical Agdal base, and a medina riad.

card1.name: Hotel Tour Hassan
card1.desc: Classic address near Hassan Tower and the administrative centre — polished rooms and a central base for monuments.

card2.name: Hotel Oudaïas
card2.desc: Stay with easy access to the Kasbah of the Udayas and Bouregreg views — practical for the historic shore.

card3.name: Agdotel
card3.desc: Modern hotel in the Agdal district — cafés, shops and train connections nearby for a city-stay rhythm.

card4.name: Riad Dar Al Manzah
card4.desc: Charming riad inside the medina walls with authentic Moroccan hospitality and a quiet atmosphere.

booking_banner.title: Explore all stays in Rabat
booking_banner.desc: Compare live rates, read traveller reviews and discover more riads and hotels.

eat.title: Where to eat in Rabat
eat.subtitle: Medina tajines, Kasbah tea, family tables and Atlantic seafood — capital classics.

dinarjat.title: Restaurant Dinarjat
dinarjat.desc: Elegant traditional Moroccan dining in a restored medina house — tajines, pastilla and a classic Rabat address.

imprevu.title: L'Imprévu
imprevu.desc: Popular city-centre tables with a mixed menu — reliable stop between museums and the medina.

naji.title: Dar Naji
naji.desc: Lively, generous Moroccan plates — tajines, salads and a family-friendly atmosphere locals recommend.

goeland.title: Le Goéland
goeland.desc: Atlantic fish and seafood near the water — a Rabat classic for grilled catch and simple plates.

ty.title: Dar Zaki
ty.desc: Cosy medina house for home-style couscous and tajines — casual, warm and easy for families.

maure.title: Café Maure
maure.desc: Iconic mint tea and pastries on the Kasbah terraces with views over the river — a must stop.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: Tram links Rabat and Salé; taxis are plentiful. The historic core is walkable between Udayas, medina and Hassan.

bargain.title: Dress & visits
bargain.desc: Modest dress at the mausoleum; security checks are normal at official sites.

water.title: Wind & weather
water.desc: Atlantic wind can cool even in sun — a light layer helps on the kasbah terrace.

daytrips.title: Day trips from Rabat
daytrips.subtitle: Across the Bouregreg, along the coast or inland from the capital.

sale.name: Salé
sale.desc: Medina and beach just across the Bouregreg — tram or boat.

casa.name: Casablanca
casa.desc: About an hour by train — Hassan II Mosque and corniche.

kenitra.name: Kenitra & Mehdia
kenitra.desc: Coast and lagoon north of the capital.

q1.question: How many days in Rabat?
q1.answer: Two full days cover the main sights; three allow Salé, museums or a quieter beach afternoon.

q2.question: Worth it versus Marrakech?
q2.answer: Yes if you want a calmer capital, sea air, major monuments and less souk intensity.

q3.question: Airport code?
q3.answer: RBA (Rabat–Salé). Casablanca CMN is an alternative with more flights, then train to Rabat.

q4.question: Best area to stay?
q4.answer: Medina/Udayas for atmosphere, Hassan for monuments, Agdal for modern cafés and space.
